relationship_to_prior_decisions: additive evidence update; does not rewrite prior X4/X5 artifacts or V1 semantics
what_is_now_established: The prior 60m sample-size limitation is no longer the main obstacle in the five-carrier independent-source track; 60m directional metrics have at least 181 origins per carrier/direction metric.
15m is materially more stable across carriers than 60m under the unchanged 20-bar slope_t/T1=2 baseline.
60m heterogeneity persists on a longer 2026 window and is not explained away by the earlier short two-carrier sample.
A static interval-specific threshold fit on 2020 Development data does not transfer cleanly to 2026 five-carrier state semantics.
Static robust interval normalization improves some scale and carrier-dispersion diagnostics but does not consistently improve persistence/reversal semantics.
No X5D candidate strictly Pareto-dominates V1 or the other candidates on the predeclared state-semantic dispersion metrics.
scientific_implication: The unresolved 60m issue is not only interval scale; temporal/regime nonstationarity and clock/source identity are material. A future method must not force constant state occupancy and must be causal and out-of-time.
next_research_boundary: Do not fit another static T1 grid to the 2026 evaluation window.
If normalization is studied further, separate state-boundary normalization from strength-scale normalization and preserve regime information.
Prefer additional exact/governed 60m clock evidence or a causal predeclared normalization study before any representation-version decision.
